newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Oil directionless ahead of Iraq news.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Oil directionless ahead of Iraq news.

text.p: World oil prices marked time on Monday as the market wandered directionless ahead of an expected further wave of Iraqi crude exports under the terms of deal with the United Nations.
The U.N. was widely expected to "rubber stamp" Iraq's plan for aid distribution, submitted to it on Monday, a precursor for further exports.
Baghdad is set to resume pumping for the third three-month period to earn a further $1 billion allowed to it to fund humanitarian aid.
By 1606 GMT Brent crude oil, the world benchmark grade, was three cents lower at $18.09 per barrel on the London futures market.

Because of delays caused by the discussion of the technicalites of aid distribution, traders feared Iraq will have to increase the flow of oil to around 1.5 million barrels per day in the time remaining to make up its revenue, around double the rate from the earlier tranches of exports.
This would depress oil prices which have already fallen by around 25 percent this year.
The current period began on June 8 but Iraq has delayed exporting oil for two months.
Brokers said the imminent U.N. approval of Baghdad's plan was likely to cause few ripples in the market.

However, London-based GNI research said in a report that while the green-light for the oil sale was fully expected by the market, the fact that the go-ahead could mean Iraqi oil shipments in the next couple of weeks meant there should still be a reaction.
"Perhaps the most bearish aspect of the Iraqi deal is the need to compress $1 billion worth of sales into a five to six week period," the GNI report said.
